primary_sources.name: AutoWorldModel-Bench: A State-Centric Benchmark for Automated World-Model Research
observed_mechanisms: architecture-agnostic evaluator with explicit adapter boundary
teacher-forced h=1 evaluation separated from open-loop rollout
open-loop horizons 10 and 20 expose error accumulation
state-centric scoring against exact structured ground truth rather than video realism
scenario tests probe rule-consistent dynamics under controlled initial state and action sequence
per-horizon decomposition prevents one-step accuracy from hiding long-horizon failure

primary_sources.name: How Should World Models Be Evaluated? A Decision-Making-Centric Position
observed_mechanisms: evaluation claims should match intended use
interventional/counterfactual action fidelity is more decision-relevant than visual plausibility
closed-loop rollout validity, reward/value prediction, policy-ranking agreement, exploitability and uncertainty calibration are distinct evidence levels

primary_sources.name: ForecastBench-Sim: A Simulated-World Forecasting Benchmark
observed_mechanisms: structured world snapshot -> future-state forecast -> simulator resolution
paired intervention worlds enable conditional/causal discrimination with immediately resolvable ground truth
simulated worlds make rare/disruptive outcomes reproducibly testable

primary_sources.name: PlayWorld: Benchmarking World Models with Agent Players over Long-Horizon Objectives
observed_mechanisms: long-horizon objectives can be more informative than fixed action strings when valid action paths differ
persistent-state evolution and out-of-sight evolution are explicit failure dimensions

recommended_order: Do not block the narrow WP803 generation-1 next-observation contract if its existing tests remain valid.
Add a later generation or follow-on benchmark layer that reports h=1 separately from bounded open-loop h>1 rollout accuracy.
Add deterministic scenario/intervention pairs where two worlds differ by one controlled action or hidden transition parameter; score the predicted divergence only after evaluator resolution.
If a prediction policy can emit probabilities, score calibration with a proper scoring rule rather than treating confidence text as evidence.
Keep all ground-truth transition state, paired-world outcome and score computation evaluator-only; never feed them back as policy input for the same trial.
evidence_backed_delta.thin_native_preference: Distill the evaluation geometry into F2-native deterministic benchmark contracts; do not import AutoWorldModelBench or video-world benchmark runtime stacks.

counterhypotheses: A one-step exact-match benchmark may be sufficient for the declared narrow WP803 generation-1 scope; multi-horizon and intervention tests may belong to later WP806/whole-system characterization rather than this generation.
Long-horizon rollout can conflate world-model quality with policy/action-selection errors unless the action sequence is evaluator-controlled or otherwise fixed for the prediction test.
Probability calibration adds interface and scoring complexity and should not be required until F2 has a genuine probabilistic prediction surface.
falsifiers_and_next_gates: Inspect merged/accepted WP803 generation-1 evidence before classifying any missing feature as a defect rather than an intentional scope boundary.
Under a separate E2 claim, map the smallest F2-native multi-horizon/intervention contract against WP800/WP803 identities and verify it does not duplicate WP806.
